method: Recomputed every threshold_ladder value_number by hand from the stated facts (base plus all priced options, absolute value of a modification, anticipated or actual ceiling) and re-derived correct_class and the covering tier from Army Warranting Program Policy v12 Table 1 (I = SAT; II = $500K/$1M/$5M/SaP; III = $10M/$25M/$50M/$100M; IV = $250M/$500M/Unlimited) using the greater-than-or-equal-to rule. All 40 arithmetic results and all 40 class assignments were reproduced independently and matched.

Checked every dollar threshold quoted in prose against the verified table in src/data/regulations.json: MPT $15,000; SAT $350,000; contingency SAT OCONUS $2,000,000; SaP ceiling $9,000,000 ($15,000,000 contingency); GPC overseas commercial limit $25,000 (DFARS 213.301); fair-opportunity enhanced tier $7,500,000; DoD task-order protest floor $35,000,000 (10 U.S.C. 3406(f)(1)(B)); CAS full coverage / Disclosure Statement $100,000,000; FAR Table 6-1 KO certification $900,000; DFARS Table 206-1 KO tier $10,000,000. Every quoted figure matched.

Fetched acquisition.gov only for the two areas the crosswalk does not cover: the RFO Part 13 deviation guide (BPA section number and the noncommercial scope of Part 13) and the RFO Part 32 deviation guide (32.702, 32.703-2, 32.703-3 and 32.907 confirmed unchanged from legacy numbering).

Checked every fiscal_sort statutory cite (31 U.S.C. 1301(a), 1304, 1341, 1342, 1351, 1501(a), 1502(a), 1517, 1535, 1552(a), 1553(a)-(b), 3302(b); 10 U.S.C. 2801-2805, 3133; 41 U.S.C. 7108(c); 5 U.S.C. 4503) and re-derived each bucket (Purpose / Time / Amount / No violation) from the stated facts, including recomputing every fiscal-year date calculation (FY start/end, period-of-performance start year, expired vs. closed accounts). All 36 bucket assignments were confirmed.

Node-graph check: NOT APPLICABLE to this file. games_1.json contains only threshold_ladder and fiscal_sort - both flat arrays of independent items with no nodes, no start node and no next pointers. The branching node graphs live in games.branching and the scenarios cases produced by other tasks, not here. changes.what: board point and cite line - justification approval tier
changes.why: The item said $2.9 million sits 'within the contracting officer's certification tier under both the governmentwide FAR table and the DoD table'. That is wrong on the FAR side: RFO FAR 6.104-2(b) Table 6-1 caps the contracting officer certification tier at $900,000, and only DFARS 206.104-71 Table 206-1 (DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0017 Rev. 2) runs the KO tier to $10,000,000. A candidate who repeated this at a board would be corrected. Rewrote the board point to name both tables correctly, said that Army follows the DoD table, and added the two table cites. Class and value_number unchanged (Class II, $2,900,000).
changes.before: Board point: the warrant question and the justification question are separate approvals and both have to be satisfied. At $2.9 million the justification for other than full and open competition is within the contracting officer's certification tier under both the governmentwide FAR table and the DoD table, but urgency does not excuse the warrant.

changes.what: ordering-procedures cite and one garbled sentence
changes.why: The item is a delivery order under a SINGLE-award IDIQ but cited 'RFO FAR 16.507 (ordering procedures)'. Per the verified crosswalk note, the RFO split legacy FAR 16.505: general order content and scope rules are at 16.506, while 16.507 is the fair-opportunity procedure for MULTIPLE-award contracts and does not apply here. Repointed the cite to 16.506 with a note on what 16.507 actually covers. Also fixed 'if orders on the order had priced options', which was garbled, to 'if the order itself carried priced options'. Class and value_number unchanged (Class II, $3,800,000).
changes.before: Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 and Table 1; RFO FAR 16.507 (ordering procedures).

changes.why: Cited a bare 'RFO FAR 13 (simplified procedures, blanket purchase agreements)'. Confirmed on the acquisition.gov RFO Part 13 deviation guide that Part 13 now covers NONCOMMERCIAL acquisitions at or below the SAT and that BPAs are addressed at 13.201, which also states that no individual purchase under a BPA may exceed the SAT - a rule that directly supports this item's $88,000 call. Pinned the cite to 13.201, added that rule, and flagged that a commercial BPA runs under Part 12 procedures. Class and value_number unchanged (Class I, $88,000).
changes.before: Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 and Table 1; RFO FAR 13 (simplified procedures, blanket purchase agreements).

changes.what: reporting statute in the cite line
changes.why: The scenario is an obligation exceeding a formal administrative subdivision of funds, correctly bucketed Amount and correctly cited to 31 U.S.C. 1517(a). The cite then listed 31 U.S.C. 1351 as the reporting provision. 1351 is the reporting provision for violations of 1341 and 1342; a 1517(a) violation is reported under 1517(b). Replaced 1351 with 1517(b) and kept a parenthetical explaining the distinction, because the explanation tells the candidate the violation 'is reportable' and a board member may well ask under which section. Bucket unchanged.
changes.before: 31 U.S.C. 1517(a) (obligations exceeding apportionment or administrative subdivision); 31 U.S.C. 1351; DoD FMR Volume 14 (Antideficiency Act violation procedures).

open_notes: games_1.json has no per-item flags or confidence fields. That matches the games shape in CONTRACT.md section 3 and the already-merged src/data/games.json, so it is not a defect in this file - but it means verification status for these items rides entirely on regulations.json, where every threshold is still status 'verify' rather than 'verified'. If the app renders a games item with no verification badge, that is a view-layer gap to close before the bank is called board-ready.
